title: 1990'S RETAIL DISPLAY FIGURE (...
reason: Large distinctive sculptural retail figure (1.9 m) with an unreadable incised inscription; decorators pay for this sort of piece and the maker is unknown.
findings: Four views of a tall stylised faceless figure in a long coat, scarf and wide-brimmed hat, arms crossed, in a cream-pink matte moulded material (plaster, resin or fibreglass) with faceted planes and only a nose ridge for a face. It stands on a rectangular clipped-corner glass base with a small metal clip fixing at the heel. Distinctive Art Deco influenced sculptural design, not a generic mannequin. There is faint scratched or incised writing on the left cuff, enlarged 8x to 9x with contrast boosted, but it is too faint and low resolution to read (could be a name or date). No label, stamp or maker's name seen anywhere. The 1990s and ex Myer claims cannot be verified from the photos.
condition: Generally clean, with small dark specks, scuffs and pinprick marks on the hat, shoulders and coat; a ragged edge at the heel where it meets the clip; no breaks seen. Glass base dusty and marked but appears intact.
rescore_note: Striking 1.9 m faceted Art Deco style figure on a glass base with real decorator appeal, but the maker, 1990s date and Myer link are all unproven and the cuff inscription is unreadable; bulky, so I put it in the $80-200 band with some upside. Estimate only, no live comps (search budget used up).
